01 / 04

An introduction to the financial perspective

My profile records Introduction to Business Finance, issued by Alison in October 2025, with credential ID 3998-36834668.

The honours entry describes study of the history, principles, and investment analysis tools of business finance. The course is included once in this learning record, even though it appears in two profile sections.

The connection

Finance is relevant to my interest in corporate law because I want to understand the commercial setting around a decision.

Read the deeper context+

A transaction is more meaningful to study when its purpose and financial assumptions are considered alongside the formal steps. This course is introductory context, not evidence of professional financial analysis.

02 / 04

Questions beyond a headline

When reading about a company or investment, I want to ask what the business is trying to achieve and which assumptions support the decision.

What is expected to create value? Which uncertainties might change the outcome? What information would a reader need before reaching a stronger conclusion?

The connection

Those questions are particularly relevant to my interests in mergers and acquisitions and private equity.

Read the deeper context+

They are areas I hope to study in more depth. I have not worked on transactions or advised investors, and the portfolio does not treat a short finance course as equivalent to that experience.

03 / 04

Building a useful foundation

My business administration course offers an organisational perspective; this course adds a financial one.

The two can help me read a commercial development with more structure. My task is to become clearer about what I understand, what I can support with a source, and what needs further explanation.

The connection

A practical next step would be to follow one public business development over time and separate its stated objectives, available information, and unanswered questions.

Read the deeper context+

That exercise would help turn introductory learning into better research habits without presenting it as investment advice or a professional valuation.
